name: gas_engine_full_power_cpbar
title: Full-power operating point of a 4-stroke gas engine (combustion products with cpbar)
summary: Steady-state energy and mass balances of a 4-stroke gas engine at its nominal operating point: throttle, isentropic path from the throttled state to the intake flow state (kinetic-energy balance), combustion in which the products are described by their mean specific heat cpbar (routine of the ULiege combustion library, copied from CSL-0005), isentropic expansion and cooling by the water jacket.

authors: ULiege MSTh course (J. Lebrun, V. Lemort, S. Bertagnolio)
origin.course: ULiege MSTh, machines et systemes thermiques, repetition TP 08 (exercise 4 of 2005-11-14)

verification.reference: EES stored solution of the original (69 variables, EES X7.458, parametric run with W_dot_sh = 0 and P_2 = 17945.38 Pa)
verification.notes: compare_solution.py (rtol = 0.001): '69 common variables, 3 differ'. t_6/t_7 (0.084 %, 1.7 K: they follow the mean specific heat c_p_g_6 of the products, +0.086 %, EES vs CoolSolve ideal-gas species enthalpies; the point is also degenerate, t_7 = t_6, see README) and the cpbar outputs / cooling terms derived from them (<= 0.09 %); the exercise results P_2, p_3, p_4, v_3, v_4, V_dot_3, t_3, Q_dot_gw, Q_dot_wa, t_w_ex_1, t_w_ex, W_dot_in_act, W_dot_p, W_dot_m <= 6.2e-6 (Q_dot_1 4.4e-4). Two deviations remain: c_f = CP(CH4, 20 C) 2220.6 vs 2241.7 J/kg-K (0.94 %, EES ideal-gas CH4 vs CoolProp) and Q_dot_2 (2.57 vs 2.59 W) which follows it; s_2 = 4360.94 vs 6175.19 J/kg-K is a constant entropy reference-state offset (EES Air table vs CoolProp Air): all entropy-derived results (t_3, v_3, C_3) agree. Needs the shipped .initials (EES guesses) and coolsolve.conf (tolerance 1E-4, see README).
